result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password or Bitwarden**\.

My overall pick is 1Password if ease of use and team collaboration matter most. Bitwarden is the better choice if keeping costs down is a priority.

## My top 4 recommendations

![Get to know 1Password for Mac | 1Password Support](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/C4U7UvvWr1lsit0fdwRMADZs7wYIji_AIA_d_hCeSHTTS1dPoJwwNeSzAPqWszRkpvDsM-p6I-6bznHJsD41eDQWYBj0MySy4qOfvgyzlD_4z3rPSGN9LVxo1hBQTb8qLml3yarSFkZEwcSqyJe7UAnBKtGHsXMSYuWNAwGS3UO1kE8Ogcbnaa14C9ioehoa?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password Business**

(Best overall)

# \$8.99

USD / user / month, annual billing

- Excellent user experience.
- Shared vaults with granular permissions.
- Strong admin controls and reporting.
- Great for onboarding and offboarding employees.

Best for teams that want something polished and easy to adopt.

[1Password business plans](https://1password.com/business)

---

![The best password managers in 2026 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/NzVuMgIchg5mHs-Kr9143cu9YVcLD78U-cfqnnpzpdksR6kB5LPVR6OyqUe0J0PAWilFgVX5RafeZ-AzNa_G6WUPgI8J1U4oAahEfqnQQL2SaxhVwFg9jy1o1kVewXMyq40iQ1cCkpkzpsh_DQntfgs6e3PLRpQFbO3dRcV-HQGbTSkVwYxuDvCJM657Aw6_?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden Teams**

(Best value)

# \$4

USD / user / month, annual billing

- Open-source foundation.
- Shared collections and organizational management.
- Audit and event logs.
- Good administrative features for the price.

Best for budget-conscious teams and technically minded organizations.

[Bitwarden business plans](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

# \$2

USD / user / month, Business Starter annual billing

- Shared folders.
- Centralized administration.
- Strong security and compliance features on higher tiers.

Best for small teams looking for an inexpensive starting point.

[Keeper business plans](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

---

![Test Dashlane : un gestionnaire de mots de passe élégant et complet, mais trop avare - Les Numériques](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/66TJUMmYmc2uHzIsxHHiAx7hxRQ8alP8a248IQqZpKMw5qyY_k9MeFr4rutufsLjTYxUl32XmJycQKSNVtCaRTxRhBdFKuuN8SD7uZ8vs9JkSCZSzdZ2yIQm88TGjWCrg-h07fJdRP7X6VdOalsZe2e6fj_Ou1dMYyLIEbt_d4hajtzL8hVlKJz2qWk0Hm2z?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Dashlane**

# \$8

USD / user / month, indicative annual pricing

- Password health monitoring.
- Phishing protection features.
- Administrative controls and security reporting.

Best for teams wanting additional credential-risk monitoring.

[Dashlane business plans](https://www.dashlane.com/business)

Pricing is indicative, in USD, before tax. Confirm current regional pricing and feature availability before purchasing. ## Quick comparison

| Feature | 1Password | Bitwarden |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Ease of use | Excellent | Very good |
| Shared passwords | Yes | Yes |
| Admin controls | Excellent | Very good |
| Audit logs | Yes | Yes |
| Open source | No | Yes |
| Value | Good | Excellent |


## What I'd look for in a team password manager

Regardless of which one you choose, make sure it supports\:

1. **Shared vaults\:** Share company credentials without sending passwords over Slack or email.
2. **Role-based permissions\:** Restrict access to sensitive accounts.
3. **Employee offboarding\:** Revoke access immediately when someone leaves.
4. **MFA\:** Require multifactor authentication.
5. **Audit logs\:** See who accessed or changed shared credentials.
6. **Personal and business separation\:** Keep employees' personal passwords separate from company credentials.

## My recommendation

I'd narrow it down to 1Password and Bitwarden.

To make a more precise recommendation, I have two questions\:

**1\. How many people are on your team?**
